correctness.rationale: Two independent exhaustive standard-library Python verifiers construct all sixteen graph distances by distinct methods, exclude resolving sets of sizes below four, and agree on all 144 rook and 48 Shrikhande metric bases. The second program proves full equality of each family to its explicit closed description. Both compute every pairwise exchange and verify 16 components of H(2,3) for rook, 48 isolated Shrikhande bases, and two-exchange connected regular graphs with degrees 26/10, edges 1872/240, and diameter three from every root. The capacity-six simulation uses only monotonicity of resolving sets; capacity-five paths among four-element optima imply one-element exchange. All graph and cardinality boundaries explicit; computational certificate sources and outputs are embedded and fully finite.

value.rationale: A natural structural question is whether minimum graph-metric landmark sets can be relocated without losing distance resolution. The two distinct strongly regular graphs share (16,6,2,2) and beta=4 but have opposite one-exchange mobility (16 nine-state grid components versus 48 frozen states), proving those classic parameters insufficient for mobility. The sharp common capacity-six threshold and connected exact two-exchange diameters give a nontrivial resilience benchmark and complete finite classification beyond published dimension/rook-basis table deductions.
